- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67 followed by +0.33), model often overcorrects downward — adjust downward bias by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.67 or -1.00) and news volume drops to 0 or low, model often fails to adjust — add 3–5% downward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment is flat or volatile (±0.33 or ±0.00) and news volume is low, model tends to drift — apply mean reversion to forecast by 1–3% toward recent 7-day average.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3–5% gap over 3+ days), model may be overestimating sentiment impact — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days if sentiment remains unchanged.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% to account for sentiment lag.
